Number Guessing

Place ValueParityAlgorithms
Game: The computer shows you a card full of numbers and works out the number you are thinking of.
How to play: Think of a number from 1 to 99. Press Yes if you can see it on the card, or No if you cannot, and keep answering until the computer says your number.
Card 1 of 7

Look for the math

The trick looks like mind reading, but the computer is simply writing your number in binary, one digit at a time. Each card asks about one digit.

Seven cards are enough

Every number below 100 fits in seven binary digits, because (1111111)2 = 27 − 1 = 127, which is bigger than 100. Six digits only reach 63, so seven is the smallest number of cards that can cover 1 to 99. The logic test checked all 99 numbers: each one needs at most seven digits, and the applet never prints 0 or 100 on a card.

One answer, one digit

Card k shows exactly the numbers whose place value 2k is switched on, or exactly those with it switched off — the computer picks which at random. The rightmost card is about parity: odd numbers have a 1 there. Yes keeps the digit on the card; No takes the other one. Either way, one answer fixes one digit. After seven answers the digits add up to your number: for instance 54 is 110110, with 0 in the ones place and 1 in the third place from the right.

What the test confirmed

The logic test replayed the applet's own card-drawing and answer code, then played all 99 possible secrets against all 128 possible runs of random cards — 12,672 games — and the computer guessed correctly every time. The page's two example groups (1, 2, 3, 8, 9, 10, 11, 16, 17 with a 0 in the third place, and 4, 5, 6, 7, 12, 13, 14, 15, 20 with a 1) were verified too. One quirk stays: if you answer inconsistently, the computer can announce 0 or a number up to 127, because it only adds the bits you gave it and never checks your number was really on the cards.

Try pressing No to every card. The computer announces the opposite of every card it showed, which can be a number that never appeared on any card — even 0 if all seven cards showed a 1. Can you work out why?
